messages:
incident-bot: ALERT - High error rate: api.redwood.com origin reachability errors observed via Cloudflare edges (us-east-1 cluster). Service: Hosted API. Symptoms: TLS handshake failures, 502/523/524 spikes, increased latency. Pager -> oncall-sre (maria).

maria (oncall-sre): seeing it in the dashboards too. spikes in 524 and TLS handshake errors from Cloudflare edge IPs. Rolling error rate up to 18% for text-generation endpoints.

ajohnson (oncall-sre): confirming. curl to api.redwood.com times out during handshake. tried from us-east ec2:

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/generate
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.com/generate
* Trying 104.16.0.1:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.com (104.16.0.1) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: 
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert internal error
```

samir (eng-runtime): I see request queue growth and a lot of connection resets. Origin (ALB) healthy. No obvious CPU/GPU issues on model hosts. This looks like edge/terminating TLS or routing at Cloudflare.

lee (network): DNS looks correct (CNAME -> our.cloudflare.net). dig reveals some CF edge addresses failing handshake. traceroute shows packets reaching CF PoP then stalling.

```
$ dig api.redwood.com +short
our-subdomain.cloudflare.net.
104.16.0.1
104.16.0.2

$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com
CONNECTED(00000005)
140735...:error:14094438:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:
```

tia (support): getting multiple customer reports via Slack/email. Some enterprise customers see 502s and TLS errors in their browser stacks. We should post a status page message ASAP.

oliver (incident-commander): Sev2 for now until we know scope. Maria you own technical lead. Tia you own comms. Samir and Lee, pair on mitigation. Aj will be backup. I'll escalate externally if CF doesn't confirm in 10m.

maria (oncall-sre): started runbook: 1) check Cloudflare status page & API 2) gather edge IPs / error rates 3) try bypass routing for high priority customers 4) lower DNS TTL and prepare ALB direct fallback if needed.

samir (eng-runtime): Cloudflare status API shows degraded TLS service in "N. America" (limited info). Opening ticket with CF support now — attaching curl diagnostics and openssl output.

```
$ curl -s https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/XXXX/diagnose -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
{ \"result\": { \"tls\": \"degraded\" }}
```

cloudflare-support-bot: Support case created #1234567. Assigned to CF Edge Ops. ETA: initial triage 15m. Links: https://support.cloudflare.com/cases/1234567

lee (network): Preparing DNS plan: we have two options: A) switch api.redwood.com CNAME to the origin-ttl-bypass subdomain (direct to ALB) and set short TTL, B) update Cloudflare load balancing fallback to route to aws-alb pool (if configured). Changing CNAME is fastest.

maria (oncall-sre): we need to consider customer certs / SNI. Direct ALB uses our cert (via ACM) so TLS should be fine. But we need to open ACLs for CF IPs? No, we want to bypass CF entirely. Prep Route53 change ready.

tia (support): drafting status page msg: short, honest, "We are experiencing TLS handshake and edge routing failures via our CDN provider Cloudflare causing intermittent API reachability issues. We are investigating and have mitigation steps in progress." Will post when given go.

ajohnson (oncall-sre): I've prepared Route53 CLI command for quick swap:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{\"Changes\": [{\"Action\": \"UPSERT\",\"ResourceRecordSet\": {\"Name\": \"api.redwood.com.\",\"Type\": \"A\",\"AliasTarget\": {\"HostedZoneId\": \"ZALB\",\"DNSName\": \"internal-api-alb-123456.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com\",\"EvaluateTargetHealth\": false}}}] }'
```

samir (eng-runtime): before we flip, let's reduce the TTL to 60s so rollback is faster if needed. Also prepare traffic-slice for priority customers so we only route sensitive tenants to ALB.

oliver (incident-commander): agree. Maria, if CF hasn't confirmed stabilization in 15 minutes, proceed with TTL change + partial switch for top 5 enterprise customers. Tia hold on external comms until we confirm the change.

maria (oncall-sre): doing TTL change now (Route53).

```
# change TTL
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{\"Changes\": [{\"Action\": \"UPSERT\",\"ResourceRecordSet\": {\"Name\": \"api.redwood.com.\",\"Type\": \"CNAME\",\"TTL\": 60,\"ResourceRecords\": [{\"Value\": \"our-subdomain.cloudflare.net.\"}]}}] }'
```

cloudflare-support-bot: CF Edge Ops: "We are investigating an internal configuration propagation issue affecting TLS termination at a subset of PoPs in North America. Mitigation actions underway."

maria (oncall-sre): CF reports partial mitigation; still seeing errors but reduced. I'm going to bring up direct ALB fallback for the 5 affected customers now.

tia (support): posting initial status page update (prelim).

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE posted to status.redwood.com - "Investigating: CDN provider Cloudflare is experiencing TLS and edge routing issues affecting API reachability in parts of North America. We are working on mitigations including DNS TTL reduction and partial routing to direct origin."

ajohnson (oncall-sre): partial routing live for customers A,B,C — verified via synthetic checks. Their error rates dropped from ~20% -> <1% after switch.

samir (eng-runtime): rollouts look good. For customers still on CF, requests still sporadically fail but at lower rate. CF says they deployed a fix and are monitoring.

lee (network): monitoring BGP / traceroutes. Cloudflare PoP health improving and route flaps reducing.

oliver (incident-commander): good. Tia start customer notification emails for affected enterprise tenants with the workaround and timeline. Assign postmortem to Maria + Samir + Lee.

maria (oncall-sre): handing to ajohnson for next shift - it's 23:40 UTC and my shift ends. Aj, take ownership for the next 2 hours to monitor CF stabilization and rollback plan if needed.

ajohnson (oncall-sre): taking over. I have the runbook and access to DNS. I'll keep the incident channel updated every 10m and escalate if errors rise above 5%.

cloudflare-support-bot: CF Edge Ops: "Root cause identified: configuration propagation bug affecting TLS termination with certain SNI patterns. Fix deployed globally. Monitoring for regressions." Case updated.

incident-bot: ACTION - Set incident severity -> Reduced to Sev3 (mitigation in place, partial customer routing).

maria (oncall-sre): thanks team, going offline.

ajohnson (oncall-sre): still watching. will coordinate with CF if we see any regression.

samir (eng-runtime): recommend follow-up items: - Add Cloudflare health webhooks to our observability - Add automated fallback routing for enterprise customers - Evaluate alternate CDN routing and DNS failover policies - Postmortem and lessons learned.

tia (support): customer comms sent to affected tenants. No escalations yet.

ajohnson (oncall-sre): last check at 23:54 UTC: error rates stable ~0.5% global, affected customers on ALB at 0.1%. Leaving channel open for 1hr, then archive.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (follow-up: postmortem assigned).

oliver (incident-commander): thanks all. Please add detailed timeline and any config changes to the postmortem doc.

maria (oncall-sre): will draft postmortem first pass tomorrow.

-- end of thread --
